subject: DPA: telemetry & runtime data exposure carveout — product + security signoff needed
messages:
From: John Halvorsen <john.halvorsen@datascope.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@datascope.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: telemetry/runtime carveout (v3)

Tessa — attaching our redline (v3). We appreciate Redwood agreeing to limit telemetry, but legal is pushing for a runtime-carveout that explicitly allows DataScope to request output-level metadata for troubleshooting and analytics. Our requested clause narrows telemetry to "error and performance metadata necessary for debugging the service used by DataScope."

Key asks from our side:
- Explicit permission to receive per-request outcome metadata for incidents (no raw PII).
- A retention cap of 30 days on any exported telemetry for our use.
- A mechanism to request temporary export beyond 30 days with joint approval.

We marked the redline in the attached PDF. Please let us know if this is plausible operationally — if not, outline the blockers and an alternative.

Thanks,
John Halvorsen
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataScope

Attachments: DataScope_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: John Halvorsen <john.halvorsen@datascope.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: telemetry/runtime carveout (v3)

John — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Quick internal notes and questions before we escalate to Security signoff:

1) Definition check: when you say "per-request outcome metadata" can you confirm you mean request-level status codes, latency, model-id, and non-sensitive prompt/response hashes (no raw prompt/response text)?
2) Retention: 30 days for exports is reasonable if we can ensure our runtime export tooling strips any raw text and only includes hashed identifiers and structured error fields.
3) Temporary export: we can support a joint-approval process but need an SLT or Security contact on the approval path.

Olga & Karthik — tagging you for product/serving impact:
- Is there an existing export path that can emit the subset John describes without storing raw prompts? If not, estimate dev effort (ballpark) and whether this can be implemented as a gated feature for DS only.

John — looping Legal CCed; we'll come back with a firm operational solution and Security signoff timeline.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, John Halvorsen <john.halvorsen@datascope.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: telemetry/runtime carveout (v3) — security review draft

John / Tessa — quick security/product readout. Summary: the carveout as-worded raises two primary operational risks we need to mitigate before signoff:

1) Data leakage via derived metadata: certain "hashes" or derived tokens can be reversible if small entropy inputs are used. We need a guarantee that any exported identifiers are salted with a system-wide secret and that exports show no raw prompt/response nor KV cache snapshots.

2) Incident export workflow: temporary export beyond 30 days must be auditable and gated. Proposed controls:
   - Exports limited to structured fields: request_id, model_id, timestamp, latency_ms, status_code, error_code, sanitized_error_message (no user-provided text).
   - All exported identifiers are HMAC-salted using a customer-specific key stored in KMS (non-reversible).
   - Export requests require two internal approvers (Product + Security) and generate an immutable audit trail (who, why, retention window).

Implementation notes from Serving:
- We do not currently have a one-click export that applies HMAC-salting to identifiers. Estimated dev: 3-4 sprints for a hardened path (includes KMS integration, audit trail UI, and export CLI). Minimal workaround: we can provide time-limited scoped logs via our support team (manual process) for high-severity incidents, but not as an automated customer export at the moment.

If DataScope accepts a manual, auditable Incident Export process for now, Security is willing to sign the DPA carveout with conditional language that we will ship an automated, customer-initiated export path within X sprints (Tessa: please propose X).

Neha: please add this to SOC control mapping and draft the conditional language we would need in the DPA.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Telemetry-Footprint-Impact.xlsx

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: John Halvorsen <john.halvorsen@datascope.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Legal Ops <legal-ops@datascope.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: telemetry/runtime carveout (v3) — path forward and signoff timeline

John — thanks for the patience. Short summary and proposed path forward so legal/security can incorporate into the DPA redline:

- We can accept a narrow carveout that permits delivery of "structured incident metadata" for debugging (request_id, model_id, timestamp, latency_ms, status_code, error_code, sanitized error category) with the following constraints: exported identifiers will be HMAC-salted using a customer-scoped key (non-reversible), and raw prompt/response text or KV cache snapshots are explicitly excluded.
- For now, exports will be provided via a manual, auditable Support/Eng workflow (will include who requested it, justification, and a retention window). Security requires a two-approver signoff for any export beyond 30 days.
- Product committed delivery: build customer-initiated, automated export with HMAC-salting and audit trail in 4 sprints. Karthik: please confirm roadmap slot. If timeline slips, we'll extend manual export support until GA.

Next steps:
1) DataScope Legal: accept conditional language and approve conditional carveout.
2) Redwood Legal/Security: we will provide suggested wording (Neha + Olga to send proposed clause by EOD Thu).
3) Tessa/Karthik: schedule a 30-min runbook session to align on the manual export steps for initial incidents.

John — are you OK with the manual-first approach and the 4-sprint product commitment? If yes, we'll mark this as conditionally approved and circulate the redline language.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
